entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.

entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo are taken at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do before arrival). Carry your passport when crossing borders inside Schengen.
entry.next_check: Read the Austrian Embassy Canberra's page on the bilateral agreement (its old address now returns 404).

culture-and-protocol.greetings_and_words: Austrian Business Agency: Austrians usually greet with 'Grüß Gott' rather than 'Guten Tag'; 'Servus' is informal among friends. Use formal 'Sie' with people you don't know and in business; 'du' is for friends.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Austria's currency is the Euro (EUR). Only change money at banks or other authorised dealers or withdraw cash from ATMs. Credit and debit cards are widely accepted, but some businesses may only accept cash. Declare funds of more than 10,000 euros or equivalent if you're travelling between Austria and a non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not just cash. Failure to do so will result in fines. You don't need to declare cash if you're travelling to or from another EU country.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Austria is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
An Austrian-Australian bilateral agreement on visa-free short stays exists; check its terms with the Austrian Embassy Canberra before relying on it.
